chapter: WPA band and 1930s New Orleans bands
title: Reel 3: Gordon Kirst's band, the Blue Room and Armand Hug
summary: Sal tells how Gordon Kirst was made bandleader, the first band in the Blue Room, and Armand Hug's rise as a pianist.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah, he told me that. You're on the fourth rail now. Heavens to Betsy. Yeah, I didn't know. You were telling me about Gordon Kirst before we forget it. He had the band. Yeah, yeah, see the fart there, they got help that the IJ Kirst couldn't play nothing. And Gordon was in the band, see, piano player. So they put Gordon with the baton leading the band.

So naturally, Steve got to play. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. So naturally, Steve got on me in the band to play piano. They all hung up to play piano in the band, not the Blue Room, see. I was the first band in the Blue Room, before I started going to name bands, you know, name bands. The same thing happened at the Club Forest when they had the bands out there, Juice Bidoux and Lou Yandies and bands and bands and bands and they started bringing out their young boy no name bands and bands. The same thing happened in the Blue Room. I tell you one thing about, I got to say about, about Armand Hug. He was always a good piano player for him. You know when I first heard Armand play, he had a, his books and his track, he was going to school. He came with a little cap on. And he played the piano, he took up. The piano player was on his barbade. Armand played it. Armand got on the piano. Played good piano man. Right there then, he only played good piano. So, when he graduated from the Fuen Dance Hall, he went to the Valencia on Bourbon Street, Night Club. From there, he went to the Slipper with Ambry Brunner. He and Eddie Miller. He said, I know the whole deal. He started going up.
